cim: British AI agent Nous now manages $1bn in household bills
cim_eredeti: British AI agent Nous now manages $1bn in household bills
szoveg_eredeti:
Nous, the London-built AI agent that looks after household bills, says it now manages more than $1bn in routine spending. The milestone lands less than two years after the product left beta, and a month after the company raised $17mn to expand beyond the UK.

Nous raises $17M to expand its household AI agent beyond the UK

More than 250,000 British households have handed the agent their life admin. It hunts for better deals on energy, broadband, mobile, and insurance contracts, cancels unwanted subscriptions, and sorts out warranties and returns.

The company says it manages an average of £2,866 ($3,829) of yearly spending per home, and saves a typical one £734 ($981) on its bills. Growth has run at 25% month on month since launch, it adds.

While general-purpose agents try to take on any request thrown at them, Nous bets on one vertical: bills, savings, and household admin.

The company also calls itself the first UK agent able to handle regulated tasks, such as buying insurance. It says it neither sells customer data nor makes money from advertising.

“Most personal AI agents are built for tech enthusiasts and early adopters. We built an agent for everyone else; one that gets on with the boring stuff reliably, without constant oversight.

A billion dollars of household spending shows that people can and will trust AI with important decisions, as long as it works and meets the highest levels of quality and safety. We’re proud that Nous is fulfilling this throughout homes across the UK,” Greg Marsh, founder and CEO of Nous, said.

Most personal AI agents are built for tech enthusiasts and early adopters, Marsh argues, while Nous aims at everyone else, doing the boring work reliably without constant oversight.

The fresh capital from October is earmarked for international expansion, a wider insurance remit and other financial services, and new tools for everyday admin. Nous has raised more than $30mn to date, with backers including Heartcore Capital, Mosaic Ventures, and Monzo co-founder Tom Blomfield.

Greg Marsh knows his way around a consumer startup, having founded the luxury rental business onefinestay, while his co-founders helped build Trouva and Ocado.

Their bet is that the next wave of AI adoption will come from households that just want the chores done.
